title: Indigenous (Traditional) Dairy Products
shortDescription: Dahi, paneer, khoa, rasgulla and other Indian milk sweets: principles and technology.
genZNote: Indian dairy sweets are applied food science: acid, heat, patience. Paneer vs chhana vs khoa — know which one gets pressed and which gets cooked down.

sections.heading: Product Principles
sections.body: Gujarat note: Amul butter, ghee, shrikhand, basundi and cheese reflect large-scale modernisation of traditional recipes; the Anand model of cooperatives shaped India's dairy sector.

table.caption: Indian dairy products
rows: Dahi/curd, lassi, chhash, shrikhand, misti doi
LAB culture; strained curd + sugar = shrikhand
Heat 85–90 °C milk, add citric acid or lactic acid, drain, press
Heating with stirring to ~ 55–70% solids; base for peda, burfi, gulab jamun
Kneaded chhana cooked in syrup; spongy structure
Desi method from dahi or cream

sections.heading: Technological Notes
bullets: Khoa types: pindi, dhap, danedar depending on acidity and heating.
Paneer yield ~ 16–20% from buffalo milk; sold in vacuum packs; FSSAI standard: moisture ≤ 70% and milk fat ≥ 50% of dry matter.
Quality issues: hard texture (over-heating), rubbery paneer, sandiness, microbial spoilage due to high moisture.
Mechanisation: continuous khoa makers, paneer presses, aseptic packing, MAP.
Regulation: FSSAI standards for each product; hygiene via GMP/HACCP.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Indigenous dairy products use acid coagulation, heat desiccation and fermentation to create traditional foods that are increasingly industrialised.

commonTraps: Do not say paneer is made using rennet like cheese — acid.
